source.title: Unified Description of Learning Dynamics in the Soft Committee Machine from Finite to Ultra-Wide Regimes

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. There are minor OCR/encoding artifacts, but the document is not cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies scaled dataset size and reports generalization-error curves that stay flat or decline rather than rise, challenging the more-data-can-hurt version in its tested SCM settings. It uses a theoretical annealed free-energy analysis rather than the original double-descent method.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly varies the scaled dataset size α and reports generalization error, so those results bear on V3. It does not identify αc as an interpolation threshold. The mention of double descent in the introduction and conclusion is discussion, not a test of the model-wise or epoch-wise double-descent curves. Cross-sectional plateau-height changes with K are recorded separately, but do not constitute a model-size sweep of the full curve.
record.test_reason: This is a statistical-mechanics analysis of the ReLU soft committee machine in the annealed, high-temperature limit (β→0), where α=βP/(NK). Gibbs learning at high temperature never interpolates the training set. The model therefore has no interpolation threshold, so its learning curves cannot show a near-threshold peak or a data-induced rise. The curves (a plateau, a specialization transition at αc≈2π, then εg∝1/α) concern a different phenomenon. Double descent comes up only in the introduction and conclusion, where the authors contrast their ultra-wide result with the overparameterization story. That is discussion, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Two additions: the authors frame the work around the high-temperature annealed approximation, and they conclude that the SCM picture, even for K≥N, is qualitatively distinct from the NTK regime and shows no enhanced generalization beyond a modest plateau reduction.
record.recipe_differences: A statistical-mechanics, student-teacher soft committee machine analysis using an annealed approximation and numerical free-energy minimization; it does not reproduce the original double-descent experimental method.
record.method_sensitivity: The learning-curve form depends on γ = M/N: small γ has a transition near αc ≈ 2π, while finite γ has no sharp transition and γ = 1 gives an α-independent low plateau. The approximation is less accurate deep in the specialized phase.

fits_no_version.finding: In annealed high-temperature Gibbs learning of a ReLU SCM, εg vs α shows a symmetric plateau and a second-order specialization transition at αc≈2π for γ≪1. The transition vanishes for finite γ, and εg∝1/α asymptotically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow committee machines under high-temperature Gibbs learning show monotone learning curves with a specialization transition, not a sample-wise double-descent peak.

fits_no_version.finding: The symmetric-plateau height decreases with K/M and saturates once K≥N. The authors note this is only a modest gain in the ultra-wide limit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the SCM, widening the student lowers the unspecialized-phase error plateau up to K=N, then saturates.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and use the annealed approximation; the paper says its expansion becomes inaccurate deep in the specialized regime. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not identify an interpolation threshold, so the relationship between αc and the interpolation threshold in V3 is not established.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep through an interpolation threshold; the SCM is shallow and not interpolating.
No interpolation threshold exists in the β→0 annealed setting, so a near-threshold sample-wise rise is not testable.
Label noise, regularization and multiple descent are not studied.
Effective parameter counting is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges V3' label is withdrawn. The β→0 annealed limit does not interpolate the training data, so absence of a sample-wise rise says nothing about near-interpolation behaviour. Double descent is mentioned only in the introduction and conclusion, as context and contrast.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over model size is reported to assess a fall-rise-fall curve around a training-set interpolation point; the SCM is also a shallow model.
No sweep over training epochs or training time is reported.

The paper does not identify a training-set interpolation threshold or establish that its αc is such a threshold; the reported dataset-size curves nevertheless test whether error rises over the studied α ranges.
No capacity sweep across model classes or general double-descent curve is tested.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
Label noise, regularization tuning, and triple or multiple descent are not tested.
The paper does not test whether an effective parameter count converts second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.operation_detail: Numerically minimize the annealed free energy over scaled dataset size α.
rows.measure: Generalization error εg as α varies.
rows.value: The error decreases rapidly to an unspecialized plateau, then transitions near αc ≈ 2π to a specialized phase; no rise in error with increasing α is reported.
rows.note: The authors describe the qualitative learning curve in the text; α is scaled dataset size.
rows.check: High-temperature annealed Gibbs learning has no interpolation threshold, so a V3 near-threshold rise cannot appear. The monotone curve is not evidence against V3.

rows.subject: soft committee machine (SCM)
rows.size_stated: N = 10^12; M = 10^6; K varies, including K ≥ N
rows.operation_detail: Compare symmetric-plateau heights across student-to-teacher width ratios.
rows.measure: Generalization-error plateau height versus width ratio.
rows.value: The symmetric-plateau height decreases as K/M increases, reaches its minimum when K ≥ N, and then saturates.
rows.note: This is a plateau-height comparison across widths, not a model-wise test-error sweep for double descent.
rows.check: This is a plateau-height comparison across widths in a non-interpolating regime. It is not a model-wise double-descent sweep.
